speaker: Samantha
text: Welcome to the software project course, and thank you for coming to the first session.

speaker: Samantha
text: This term you will build a real application for a real client, from the first interview to the final demo.

speaker: Samantha
text: The client for this year's project is the city library, and they need a new system for room bookings.

speaker: Samantha
text: They will join us twice during the term to review what you have built.

speaker: Rishi
text: Let me go through how the teams work.

speaker: Rishi
text: You will work in teams of four students, and we form the teams by the end of this week.

speaker: Rishi
text: Each team chooses a team lead, but the role rotates every three weeks.

speaker: Rishi
text: That way everyone gets some practice at planning and at saying no.

speaker: Rishi
text: In the first two weeks you will interview the librarians and write down what they actually need.

speaker: Rishi
text: Do not start coding before you understand the problem, it is the most common mistake we see.

speaker: Rishi
text: Write the requirements as short user stories, and check each one with the client.

speaker: Samantha
text: Now the tools, which are not optional.

speaker: Samantha
text: All code must live in the university GitLab, not on personal accounts.

speaker: Samantha
text: We look at the commit history when we grade, so commit early and commit often.

speaker: Samantha
text: Every change needs approval from two teammates before it is merged.

speaker: Samantha
text: Reviews are where most of the learning happens, so take them seriously.

speaker: Rishi
text: On testing, we have a simple rule.

speaker: Rishi
text: The target for automated test coverage is seventy percent of the code.

speaker: Rishi
text: Coverage is not quality, but a project with no tests is not finished.

speaker: Rishi
text: We will show you how to run the tests automatically on every push.

speaker: Samantha
text: Next, the rhythm of the week.

speaker: Samantha
text: There is a short stand up meeting every Monday at nine, and it takes fifteen minutes at most.

speaker: Samantha
text: Each person says what they did, what they will do next, and what is blocking them.

speaker: Samantha
text: If something is blocking you for more than a day, tell us, do not wait for the meeting.

speaker: Samantha
text: Keep a shared board with all open tasks, and move each card when its status changes.

speaker: Samantha
text: We will look at the board during the weekly meetings, so keep it honest.

speaker: Samantha
text: A board full of cards marked almost done usually means nothing is done at all.

speaker: Rishi
text: Some practical matters about money.

speaker: Rishi
text: Each team gets a budget of five hundred euros for hardware, such as tablets for testing.

speaker: Rishi
text: Keep the receipts, the finance office is very strict about them.

speaker: Samantha
text: Now the important dates.

speaker: Samantha
text: Demo day is on December the third, in the main hall, and the client will be in the audience.

speaker: Samantha
text: Each team gets ten minutes to present and five minutes for questions.

speaker: Samantha
text: Rehearse the demo at least twice, and always have a backup video in case the network fails.

speaker: Samantha
text: Show the client the thing they asked for first, and the clever extras afterwards.

speaker: Samantha
text: Every member of the team should speak during the presentation.

speaker: Rishi
text: After the demo you hand in a written report.

speaker: Rishi
text: The final report is limited to twenty pages, including figures.

speaker: Rishi
text: Shorter is fine, and clearer is always better.

speaker: Rishi
text: Late submissions lose five percent of the mark for every day they are late.

speaker: Samantha
text: That is the overview, now let us take your questions.
